lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Circles, Angles, Area, and Surface Area
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: area of composite figures

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A room shaped like an L is made from a 10-by-8 rectangle with a 3-by-2 rectangular corner cut out. What is the area of the room, in square units?

steps: Find the area of the full rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80.
Find the area of the removed corner: 3 × 2 = 6.
Subtract the corner from the rectangle: 80 − 6 = 74 square units.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 156 square units and a width of 13 units. What is its exact length, in units?
A rectangular prism has length 6, width 13, and height 8 (all in units). What is its exact surface area, in square units?
What is the exact volume of a rectangular prism with length 15, width 10, and height 7 (units)? Give your answer in cubic units.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A circle has a radius of 4 1/2 ft. What is its exact circumference? Express your answer as a multiple of π.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A circle has a circumference of 31/2π m. What is its exact radius?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A circle has a diameter of 11 in. What is its exact area? Express your answer as a multiple of π (use a fraction for the coefficient if it is not a whole number).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
